bg-17-01.hint: Please eat a lot and enjoy your meal.
bg-17-01.why: 드세요 is the special honorific and polite command form for 먹다 / 마시다.

bg-17-01.q: Write a polite sentence telling someone to read a book slowly, using 천천히 and 읽으세요.
bg-17-01.why: 읽다 has a batchim, so it attaches -으세요: 읽으세요.

steps.en: Please read the Korean book at home.

ko: 그리고 우리에게 따뜻할 때 많이 드세요라고 말씀하세요.
en: Grandmother comes to our house every weekend.
Grandmother makes delicious bulgogi in the kitchen.
And she tells us to eat plenty while it is warm.

bg-17-01.q: What does the grandmother make in the kitchen?
options: Delicious bulgogi
Cold noodles
Birthday cake
bg-17-01.why: The passage says '할머니는 부엌에서 맛있는 불고기를 만드세요' (Grandmother makes delicious bulgogi in the kitchen).

bg-17-01.q: In '할머니가 우리 집에 오세요', what function does 오세요 serve?
options: An honorific statement describing Grandmother's action
A strict command ordering someone to leave
A past-tense complaint
bg-17-01.why: When describing the action of a respected elder like 할머니, -(으)세요 functions as an honorific statement.

items: I can use -(으)세요 both for polite commands and for honorific statements/questions
I can drop ㄹ before -세요 in ㄹ-stem verbs like 만들다 (만드세요)

items.en: please look at this for me

bg-17-02.hint: Please open the window for me.
bg-17-02.why: 열다 attaches -어 주세요 to ask someone to open the window as a favor.

bg-17-02.q: Write a polite request asking someone to speak slowly for you, using 천천히 and 말해 주세요.
bg-17-02.why: 말하다 becomes 말해 주세요 when asking the listener to speak for your benefit.

steps.en: Please open the window for me.
Please open the classroom window for me.

ko: 저는 오늘 한국어 수업 시간에 모르는 표현이 있었어요.
선생님께 이 문장을 다시 한번 설명해 주세요라고 부탁했어요.
선생님이 칠판에 예문을 쓰고 친절하게 가르쳐 주셨어요.
en: Today during Korean class, there was an expression I did not know.
I politely asked the teacher to explain this sentence once more for me.
The teacher wrote an example on the board and kindly taught me.

bg-17-02.q: What did the student ask the teacher to do?
options: Explain the sentence once more
End the class early
Turn off the classroom lights
bg-17-02.why: The passage says '선생님께 이 문장을 다시 한번 설명해 주세요라고 부탁했어요' (I asked the teacher to explain this sentence once more).

bg-17-02.q: How did the teacher help the student?
options: Wrote an example on the board and taught kindly
Gave a difficult pop quiz
Sent an email the next week
bg-17-02.why: The passage states '칠판에 예문을 쓰고 친절하게 가르쳐 주셨어요' (Wrote an example on the board and kindly taught me).

items: I can ask someone to do a favor for me using -아/어 주세요
I can apply -아/어 vowel harmony accurately before 주세요

items.ex: 따뜻한 커피 한 잔 만들어 주세요.

bg-17-03.hint: Please write your name here for me.
bg-17-03.why: 쓰다 drops ㅡ before -어 주세요 to become 써 주세요.

bg-17-03.q: Write a polite request asking someone to listen to your story, using 이야기를 and 들어 주세요.
bg-17-03.why: 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) changes ㄷ to ㄹ before -어 주세요: 들어 주세요.

bg-17-03.wrong: 가방이 너무 무거운데 저 좀 돕아 주세요.
answers: 가방이 너무 무거운데 저 좀 도와주세요.
가방이 너무 무거운데 저 좀 도와주세요
bg-17-03.hint: 돕다 is a ㅂ irregular verb that changes ㅂ to 오 before -아 주세요: 도와주세요!
bg-17-03.why: 돕다 conjugates to 도와- + 주세요 → 도와주세요.

steps.en: Please call a taxi for me.
Please call a taxi to the front of the hotel for me.

ko: 할아버지가 민수에게 이 상자 좀 같이 들어 주세요라고 말씀하셨어요.
en: Grandfather was holding a large box.
Grandfather said to Minsu, 'Please carry this box together with me.'

bg-17-03.q: What did Grandfather ask Minsu to do?
options: Help carry a large box together
Call a taxi to the station
Write an address on a letter
bg-17-03.why: The passage says '이 상자 좀 같이 들어 주세요라고 말씀하셨어요' (Asked him to carry the box together).

bg-17-03.q: How did Minsu respond to Grandfather's request?
options: He gladly helped him
He said he was too busy
He went inside to sleep
bg-17-03.why: The passage states '민수는 기쁜 마음으로 할아버지를 도와드렸어요' (Minsu gladly helped Grandfather).

items: I can form polite requests with irregular verbs like 도와주세요, 들어 주세요, and 불러 주세요
I can distinguish regular consonant verbs like 닫아 주세요 from ㄷ-irregular verbs like 들어 주세요

items.en: please take a seat (for your comfort)
please sit down (as a favor to me)
please stop the car for me

bg-17-04.hint: Please take me to the airport.
bg-17-04.why: Asking a driver to take you somewhere is a request for your benefit, so use 가 주세요.

bg-17-04.q: Write a polite sentence asking someone to close the door for you because it is noisy, using 닫아 주세요.
bg-17-04.why: Closing the door benefits the speaker, so use -아/어 주세요 (닫아 주세요).

bg-17-04.wrong: 택시 기사님, 지금 서울역으로 가아 주세요.
answers: 택시 기사님, 지금 서울역으로 가 주세요.
택시 기사님, 지금 서울역으로 가 주세요
bg-17-04.hint: 가다 ends in ㅏ, so -아 merges: 가 + 아 → 가. Say 가 주세요.
bg-17-04.why: 가아 주세요 is wrong: when the stem ends in ㅏ, -아 merges into it, giving 가 주세요.

bg-17-04.h: General Directive -(으)세요 vs Favor Request -아/어 주세요

a.d: Directs or invites the listener for their own comfort or as general etiquette.
ex: 손님, 여기 편하게 **앉으세요**. / Customer, please sit here comfortably.

b.d: Politely asks the listener to perform an action for the speaker's benefit.
ex: 기사님, 서울역으로 **가 주세요**. / Driver, please take me to Seoul Station.
추우니까 창문 좀 **닫아 주세요**. / Since it is cold, please close the window for me.

bg-17-04.tip: Ask yourself who benefits: if it is for the listener's own good, use -(으)세요; if you are asking a favor for yourself, use -아/어 주세요.

base.en: Please stop the car for me.

steps.en: Please stop the car in front of the station for me.
Driver, please stop the car in front of the station for me.

ko: 택시 기사님께 한국병원 앞으로 가 주세요라고 말했어요.
내릴 때 기사님이 지민 씨에게 조심히 가세요라고 인사하셨어요.
en: Jimin took a taxi in the morning.
She said to the taxi driver, 'Please take me to the front of Hankuk Hospital.'
When getting off, the driver greeted Jimin, 'Please go safely.'

bg-17-04.q: Why did Jimin say '가 주세요' to the taxi driver?
options: Because she was asking the driver to take her to the hospital
Because she wanted the driver to go home alone
Because she was asking about the driver's hobby
bg-17-04.why: Jimin used 가 주세요 because driving her to the hospital is a service done for her.

bg-17-04.q: What did the driver say to Jimin when she got off?
options: Please go safely (조심히 가세요)
Please close the window (창문을 닫아 주세요)
Please wait a moment (잠깐 기다려 주세요)
bg-17-04.why: The passage says '기사님이 지민 씨에게 조심히 가세요라고 인사하셨어요' (The driver greeted Jimin, 'Please go safely').

items: I can distinguish clearly between -(으)세요 (for the listener) and -아/어 주세요 (for the speaker)
I can use natural expressions in taxis, restaurants, and classrooms
